files.lesson.md: --- order: 19 unit: products10 node: AC9M10A01 n3 uses: [AC9M9A02 n1, AC9M9A02 n2, AC9M9A02 n3] assumes: [AC9M9A02 n1, AC9M9A02 n2, AC9M9A02 n3, AC9M10A01 n2] # n2 (negative powers with letters) is taught in Real numbers, Year 10 connection: mental-shortcut title: Special products summary: "A square bracket has two strips and a corner, so (x − 3)² = x² − 6x + 9, not x² − 9. And (x + a)(x − a) has strips that cancel, leaving x² − a²." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "Can you square 51 in your head, and work out 49 × 51, with no calculator?" app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8351 url: http://127.0.0.1:8351/index.html readySelector: "#sl-p" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: special.yml#explain-pic, caption: "$(x - 3)^2$: the square $x^2$, two red strips of $3x$ taken off, and a corner of $+9$." } explainClip: query: { code: "@special.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "A square bracket: two strips and a corner" say: "A bracket squared makes a square with two strips and a corner." clip: - caption: { text: "(x + 2)(x + 2): x², two strips of 2x, and a corner of 4.", say: "x plus two, times x plus two, is a square, two strips and a corner." } - wait: 900 - expect: { selector: "#tsum", contains: "x² + 4x + 4" } - caption: { text: "Make both numbers −2: the strips turn red, the corner stays +4.", say: "Make both numbers minus two. The strips turn red, but the corner stays positive." } - click: Make p smaller - click: Make p smaller - click: Make p smaller - click: Make p smaller - click: Make q smaller - click: Make q smaller - click: Make q smaller - click: Make q smaller - expect: { selector: "#tsum", contains: "x² − 4x + 4" } - wait: 1400 --- Try $51 \times 51$ in your head. Then try $49 \times 51$. Most people reach for a phone, but a few can do both in a couple of seconds, and it isn't a memorised table. It's a picture, and the picture still works when the number is a letter. ## Predict: the lawn ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to the area of a lawn with a strip taken off two sides shows who squares each term ((x − 3)² = x² − 9) and who sees two strips and a corner." check: type: predict q: "A square lawn is $x$ metres each way. A path 3 m wide takes a strip off two sides, so the lawn that's left is $x - 3$ metres each way. Which expression is its area?" options: - "$x^2 - 6x + 9$" - "$x^2 - 9$" - "$x^2 - 6x - 9$" - "$x^2 - 3x + 9$" actual: "x² − 6x + 9. Start with the whole x by x square and take off the two strips of 3x. The 3 by 3 corner was in both strips, so it's been taken off twice: put 9 back. x² − 9 only squares each part; x² − 6x − 9 forgets to put the corner back." ``` The council wants a path along two sides of the lawn. What area of lawn is left? Make a guess before you build it. ## Run: take the strips off ```step stage: run insight: "Taking a strip off each side of a square leaves the corner taken off twice, so the corner has to come back: two strips and a corner, not just a square." try: { playground: board, starter: "special.yml#run", height: 600 } check: { type: board, text: "Set the board to $(x - 3)(x - 3)$. Which pieces are red, and what's the corner? Was your prediction right?", when: "p = -3 and q = -3" } ``` $p$ and $q$ are the numbers in the brackets. Make both of them $-3$: the red strips are the path, and the board shows what's left. ## Investigate: two strips and a corner ```step stage: investigate insight: "A squared bracket is the bracket times itself, so every term multiplies every term: two strips and a corner, never just x² plus the square of the number. Dev squares each term and drops the strips." tasks: - check: type: answer q: "Expand $(x + 6)^2$. Type $x^2$ as x^2." answer: "x^2 + 12x + 36" form: expanded feedback: - ["x^2 + 36", "That leaves out the two strips. (x + 6)² is (x + 6)(x + 6): four pieces."] - ["x^2 + 6x + 36", "There are two strips of 6x, not one."] - ["x^2 + 12x + 12", "The corner is 6 × 6, not 6 + 6."] explain: "x² + 6x + 6x + 36 = x² + 12x + 36." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#dev" text: "Dev expands $(x - 4)^2$. Click the line where his working goes wrong." answer: 4 fault: logic misconception: binomial-two-terms explain: "Line 4: Dev left out the two strips, −4x and −4x. (x − 4)(x − 4) = x² − 4x − 4x + 16 = x² − 8x + 16." - check: type: question q: "Why does $(x + 6)(x - 6)$ have no $x$ term?" options: ["The two strips are +6x and −6x, so they cancel", "6 and −6 are small numbers", "Both brackets start with x", "There's only one strip when the signs differ"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "The size of the numbers doesn't matter: 7 and −7 would do the same.", "That's true of every pair of brackets here, and most of them have an x term.", "There are always two strips. One is red."] explain: "x² − 6x + 6x − 36: the strips are opposites, so they add to nothing and the answer is x² − 36." ``` ### Square a bracket Here's one worked out, piece by piece. ```worked (x + 4)^2 :: Means (x + 4)(x + 4): a square, x + 4 each way. x \times x = x^2 :: The big square. x \times 4 = 4x :: One strip. 4 \times x = 4x :: The other strip, the same size. 4 \times 4 = 16 :: The corner. x^2 + 4x + 4x + 16 = x^2 + 8x + 16 :: Collect the two strips. ``` Now try one on paper, piece by piece like the example: $(x + 6)^2$. Then type your answer. ### Find the mistake Read Dev's working. How many pieces should there be? ### No x term Back to $(x + 6)(x - 6)$ on the board. Look at the two strips. ## Modify: one change at a time ```step stage: modify insight: "One change at a time: a negative square, strips that cancel, spotting a perfect square, and a number in front of x." try: { playground: board, starter: "special.yml#vary", height: 620 } tasks: - hint: ["Set p and q both to −5. Both strips are red.", "The corner is −5 × (−5)."] check: { type: answer, q: "Expand $(x - 5)^2$.", answer: "x^2 - 10x + 25", form: expanded, feedback: [["x^2 - 25", "That leaves out the two strips. (x − 5)² is (x − 5)(x − 5)."], ["x^2 + 10x + 25", "Both strips are red: −5x and −5x."], ["x^2 - 10x - 25", "A negative times a negative is positive: the corner is +25."]], explain: "x² − 5x − 5x + 25 = x² − 10x + 25." } smaller: check: { type: "answer", q: "Just the two strips: what's $-5x$ and $-5x$ together?", answer: "-10x", explain: "Both strips are negative: −5x − 5x = −10x." } - hint: ["Set p to 9 and q to −9.", "What happens to the two strips?"] check: { type: answer, q: "Expand $(x + 9)(x - 9)$.", answer: "x^2 - 81", form: expanded, feedback: [["x^2 + 81", "9 × (−9) is −81."], ["x^2 - 18x - 81", "The strips are +9x and −9x. They cancel."], ["x^2 - 9", "The corner is 9 × 9 = 81, not 9."]], explain: "x² − 9x + 9x − 81 = x² − 81. The strips cancel." } - hint: ["Try the strips: do they add to the middle number?", "A perfect square has two equal strips and a corner that's a square."] check: type: question q: "Which of these is a bracket squared, like $(x + a)^2$ for some number $a$?" options: ["$x^2 + 10x + 25$", "$x^2 + 10x + 16$", "$x^2 + 25$", "$x^2 - 25$"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "16 is a square, but two strips of 4x make 8x, not 10x.", "A squared bracket always has two strips. Without them it's not (x + a)²: the strips would be 0.", "That's (x + 5)(x − 5), two different brackets with strips that cancel."] explain: "x² + 10x + 25 is (x + 5)(x + 5): two strips of 5x and a corner of 25. Half the middle number, squared, gives the last: (10 ÷ 2)² = 25." - hint: ["Set a and b to 2 and p and q to 3.", "$2x \\times 2x$ is $4x^2$, not $2x^2$."] check: { type: answer, q: "Edge case: expand $(2x + 3)^2$.", answer: "4x^2 + 12x + 9", form: expanded, feedback: [["4x^2 + 9", "That leaves out the two strips. (2x + 3)² is (2x + 3)(2x + 3)."], ["2x^2 + 12x + 9", "2x times 2x is 4x²: 2 × 2 and x × x."], ["4x^2 + 6x + 9", "There are two strips of 6x: 12x."]], explain: "4x² + 6x + 6x + 9 = 4x² + 12x + 9." } ``` ### A negative square ### Strips that cancel ### Is it a square? ### A number in front of x ## Practise: expand and spot ```step stage: practise insight: "Squares and differences of squares, mixed, with the review keeping factorising a pair of numbers fresh." tasks: - check: type: answer q: "Expand $(x + 8)^2$." answer: "x^2 + 16x + 64" form: expanded feedback: - ["x^2 + 64", "(x + 8)² is (x + 8)(x + 8): four pieces, with two strips of 8x."] explain: "x² + 8x + 8x + 64 = x² + 16x + 64." - check: type: answer q: "Expand $(x - 7)^2$." answer: "x^2 - 14x + 49" form: expanded feedback: - ["x^2 - 49", "That's what (x − 7)(x + 7) makes. (x − 7)² has two red strips."] - ["x^2 + 14x + 49", "Both strips are red: −7x and −7x."] - ["x^2 - 14x - 49", "−7 × (−7) is +49."] explain: "x² − 7x − 7x + 49 = x² − 14x + 49." smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "Just the corner: what's $(-7) \\times (-7)$?", answer: 49, explain: "A negative times a negative is positive: +49." } - check: type: answer q: "Expand $(x + 10)(x - 10)$." answer: "x^2 - 100" form: expanded feedback: - ["x^2 + 100", "10 × (−10) is −100."] - ["x^2 - 20x - 100", "The strips are +10x and −10x: they cancel."] explain: "x² − 10x + 10x − 100 = x² − 100." - check: type: question q: "Which of these is a difference of two squares: a square take away a square?" options: ["$x^2 - 64$", "$x^2 + 64$", "$x^2 - 16x + 64$", "$x^2 - 60$"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "That's a sum: a square plus a square. It has no pair of brackets that gives it.", "That's (x − 8)², a bracket squared, not a difference.", "60 isn't a square number."] explain: "x² − 64 is x² − 8², which is (x + 8)(x − 8)." - check: type: answer q: "Review: factorise $x^2 + 9x + 20$." answer: "(x + 4)(x + 5)" form: factorised feedback: - ["(x + 2)(x + 10)", "2 + 10 = 12, not 9."] explain: "4 and 5 multiply to 20 and add to 9." ``` ### A positive square ### A negative square ### The strips cancel ### Name the pattern ### Review Two numbers, from Factorising quadratics. ## Make: back to 51 × 51 ```step stage: make insight: "Coming back to the numbers: 51 is 50 + 1, so the square has two strips of 50 and a corner of 1, and 49 × 51 is (50 − 1)(50 + 1), where the strips cancel." tasks: - hint: ["Write 51 as 50 + 1 and 49 as 50 − 1.", "50 × 50 is 2500."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "Work out $51^2$ and $49 \\times 51$ with no calculator, by writing each with 50 in it. Then say how much bigger $51^2$ is." steps: - ["$51^2 = (50 + 1)^2 = 2500 + 50 + 50 + 1 = 2601$", "a square of 50, two strips of 50 and a corner of 1"] - ["$49 \\times 51 = (50 - 1)(50 + 1) = 2500 - 1 = 2499$", "the two strips are +50 and −50, so they cancel"] - ["$2601 - 2499 = 102$", "subtract"] picks: - step: 2 q: "Why is there no 50 strip left in $49 \\times 51$?" options: ["One strip is +50 and the other is −50", "49 and 51 are close to 50", "Multiplying is quicker than squaring"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "That's why it's easy to see, but not why the strips go. Look at their signs.", "The strips go because of their signs, not how quick it is."] answer: "102" answerLabel: "How much bigger" feedback: - ["100", "That's the two strips. 51² also has the corner of 1, and 49 × 51 has −1 instead: 100 + 1 + 1."] - ["2", "That's the two corners, +1 and −1. The strips add 100 as well."] criteria: - "I wrote 51 as 50 + 1 and 49 as 50 − 1." - "I found the strips (two of 50 for the square, none for the other) and the corner." - "Both my answers are close to 2500." explain: "51² = 2601 and 49 × 51 = 2499, so 51² is 102 bigger: the two strips of 50, plus the corner of +1 against −1." - check: type: question q: "Which is the quick way to work out $98 \\times 102$?" options: ["$(100 - 2)(100 + 2) = 10\\,000 - 4 = 9996$", "$(100 - 2)(100 + 2) = 10\\,000 + 4 = 10\\,004$", "$100 \\times 100 - 2 \\times 2 \\times 100 = 9600$", "$98 \\times 100 + 2 = 9802$"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "The corner is 2 × (−2) = −4: the strips cancel, but the corner stays.", "There's no strip left to take off: the strips cancel.", "102 is 100 + 2, not 100 + 2 ones tacked on after."] explain: "98 is 100 − 2 and 102 is 100 + 2, so the strips cancel and it's 100² − 2² = 9996." ``` ### The numbers Back to 51. Work this out on paper first, then type your answer. ### Another pair **Also used in** - **Mental maths.** Any two numbers the same distance either side of an easy number: $47 \times 53$, $98 \times 102$, $19 \times 21$. - **Factorising.** Run the pattern backwards: $x^2 - 49$ is $(x + 7)(x - 7)$, and $x^2 + 10x + 25$ is $(x + 5)^2$. - **Next lessons.** Factorising when there's a number in front of $x^2$, then completing the square, which is a squared bracket with the corner moved out. ```teacher summary: Students take two strips off a square lawn and see why (x − 3)² has a corner to put back, then meet the difference of two squares, where the strips cancel, and use both to square 51 and multiply 49 × 51 in their heads (AC9M10A01, node 3). time: 45 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 15 min · Modify 12 min · Practise and Make 10 min goals: - I can expand a bracket squared, with a plus or a minus, and say why there are two strips and a corner. - I can expand (x + a)(x − a) and say why there's no x term. - I can use the patterns to work out something like 49 × 51 in my head. struggle: Squaring each term and dropping the strips, and the sign of the corner when both numbers are negative. Ask students to draw the square and label the two strips before they write anything. before: > Do the Run board yourself first. Students need Two brackets, The pattern and Factorising quadratics from Year 9. The picture is the same rectangle on the tiles board; red pieces are taken away. The one idea: (x + a)² and (x − a)² are a bracket times itself, so there are two strips and a corner; (x + a)(x − a) has two strips that are opposites, so they cancel. The common mistake is squaring each term, (x − 4)² = x² + 16 (Dev's working, planted after the worked example). Hinge node: sign errors in expanding carry into factorising and completing the square. The smaller steps ask for half the move with numbers (the two strips, then the corner). If a student's strips are right and the corner is wrong, ask what a negative times a negative is. The lawn and the numbers 51, 49 and 98 × 102 are made up: no figure here is a real measurement. running: - "Predict: take a show of hands. Students who chose x² − 9 squared each term. Ask them to point to the two strips on the lawn picture." - "Run: ask students which pieces are red, and why the corner isn't." - "Investigate: draw the square for (x − 4)² live and shade the corner that was taken off twice." - "Paper: the try-one after the worked example and 51² and 49 × 51 in Make are worked on paper first. Books out, and look for 50 + 1 and 50 − 1 written out." - "Modify: before (x + 9)(x − 9), ask what the two strips will be." - "Make: before anyone writes, ask who thinks 49 × 51 is bigger than 51 × 51." stuck: - see: A student writes (x − 4)² = x² + 16 (Dev's mistake). ask: Sketch the square. How many pieces are there? fix: "Four: x², two strips of −4x and a corner of +16. Every term multiplies every term." - see: A student writes x² − 9 for (x − 3)². ask: What's (x − 3) times (x − 3), one piece at a time? fix: "x², −3x, −3x and +9: the corner is a negative times a negative." - see: A student gets (x + 6)(x − 6) = x² + 36. ask: What's 6 times −6? fix: −36. The corner is negative here, and the strips cancel. stretch: Expand (x + 2)(x² + 3x + 1) by building a bigger rectangle with an x² side, then check the answer by putting x = 1 into both sides. support: "A blank 2 by 2 grid to fill in for each product, with the brackets' terms along the top and down the side. A strip of squares: 49, 64, 81, 100, 121, 144." leads: > Starts the Year 10 expand and factorise work (AC9M10A01 node 3). Where it leads: factorising when there's a number in front of x² (next lesson), completing the square, and solving quadratics. exit: q: Expand (x − 6)². a: x² − 12x + 36. explain: > A bracket squared is the bracket times itself: $(x + 3)^2 = (x + 3)(x + 3) = x^2 + 3x + 3x + 9 = x^2 + 6x + 9$. There are four pieces: a square, two strips and a corner. It isn't $x^2 + 9$. With a minus sign, the strips are red and the corner is still positive: $(x - 3)^2 = x^2 - 6x + 9$. When the brackets differ only in their sign, the strips cancel: $(x + 3)(x - 3) = x^2 - 3x + 3x - 9 = x^2 - 9$. ```

files.working.txt:
# Dev's working for the "find the mistake" task. Plain text: students click the wrong line, nothing runs.

# region: dev
Expand (x − 4)².
(x − 4)² means (x − 4)(x − 4).
x times x is x², and −4 times −4 is 16.
So (x − 4)² = x² + 16.
# endregion
